messages:
maria: kicking off an offline replay for the new continuous-batcher heuristic. goal: understand how queue-shape + kv-warmup interplay affects token-budget targets. running on trace slice 2025-02-fractionA.

ajay: nice. what's the config? token_budget=256? dynamic_kv_warmup on?

maria: token_budget=192, queue_policy=shape-aware, kv_warmup=prefix-heuristic (warm first 64 tokens of top-10 prefixes). batch_max=128.

sasha: FYI if you lower token_budget <200 you'll shift more work into microbatches which can spike p95 unless batching joins enough callers. watch join timeout.

maria: noted. I'll also run an A/B with token_budget=256 for comparison.

perf-bot: replay started (id: r-20250218-177999). traces: 3.4M requests, avg seq=136, median sender-concurrency=3.

devon: quick profiler snapshot from the first run: kernel-switches up 12%, KV lookup hit-rate +8%, but CPU-side queue scan time increased 18ms median. logs attached to replay ID.

maria: results (A: tb=192 / B: tb=256):
- A p50=18ms p95=128ms p99=340ms
- B p50=22ms p95=95ms p99=280ms
KV hit-rate: A=62% B=58%
observations: smaller token budget reduced wasted KV work but increased scheduling fragmentation -> higher tail.

ajay: interesting tradeoff. B has higher KV misses but better p95 which implies better batch consolidation. do you have the queue-shape histograms?

maria: yes, pasted below:
```
queue_length_hist_A = {0: 19%, 1: 45%, 2: 20%, 3: 10%, 4+: 6%}
queue_length_hist_B = {0: 23%, 1: 50%, 2: 15%, 3: 7%, 4+: 5%}
```
A has more join opportunities at length=2/3, but microbatching threshold caused earlier flushes.

sasha: what about join-timeout distribution? if we relax timeout by 5ms does A improve?

maria: I fuzzed that: A +5ms join-timeout -> p95 drops from 128ms to 108ms, KV hit-rate unchanged. but p50 rises ~2ms.

devon: can we try a hybrid: token_budget=192 but adaptive join-timeout that grows when queue occupancy >2? simple rule: timeout=5ms if occ<=1 else 12ms.

maria: spun that config in the replay (C). summary C: p50=20ms p95=92ms p99=300ms, KV hit-rate=63%. much closer to B but with lower overall token work.

ajay: nice — that suggests an occupancy-aware timeout recovers tail while keeping token_budget benefits. does this change kernel selection freq?

maria: kernel selection logs: C had 7% more large-seq kernels chosen compared to A, similar to B. indicating larger formed batches allowed picking the more efficient attention kernel for long sequences.

sasha: any perf-regressions vs baseline (prod)? regression harness says p99 delta +4% on a small cohort (heavy-concat) for C.

maria: flagged that cohort for model-specific tuning. likely due to KV cold-start on concatenated prefixes. plan: add a short prefetch window for concat-heavy queries during rollout.

perf-bot: replay finished. artifacts: /replays/r-20250218-177999/ (configs, traces, profiler.csv, queue-hist.png).

devon: next steps: 1) run longer A/B on a different trace slice (2025-01-B), 2) add occupancy-adaptive join-timeout to canary, 3) build a small eval harness to exercise heavy-concat cohort and verify prefetch fix.

maria: I'll open a PR with the occupancy-timeout code and attach the replay artifacts. leaning toward rolling C into canary with the concat prefetch gated by cohort sampling.

ajay: please include the kernel-selection trace in PR so model-onboarding can see why certain kernels get chosen.

maria: will do. tagging @sasha for infra canary checklist. :thumbsup:

sasha: got it. will review infra hooks and quotas.

maria: thanks team — big win: occupancy-adaptive timeout seems to give us the best unit economics (lower token work + acceptable p95). we'll schedule the larger AB next week.
